theorySlides.title: What is Flexbox? 📦
theorySlides.content:
Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout method for rows or columns.

Key properties:
• display: flex
• justify-content (main axis)
• align-items (cross axis)
• flex-direction

theorySlides.title: Flexbox Axes 🎯
theorySlides.content:
Two axes in flexbox:

**Main Axis** - Direction items flow (row/column)
• justify-content controls this

**Cross Axis** - Perpendicular to main
• align-items controls this

theorySlides.title: Centering with Flexbox
Flex Item Properties 🔧

questions.question: Which property centers on main axis?
What does flex-direction: column do?
questions.explanation: column changes the main axis to vertical, stacking items top to bottom.

questions.question: What does flex: 1 mean?
options: Item takes equal share of space
questions.explanation: flex: 1 means flex-grow: 1, allowing the item to grow and fill available space.

codingChallenge.title: Center a Box

testCases.expectedOutput: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;

codingChallenge.hint: Use display: flex with justify-content and align-items center

theorySlides.title: CSS Grid 🔲
theorySlides.content:
CSS Grid creates layouts with rows AND columns.

Key properties:
• grid-template-columns
• grid-template-rows
• gap
• fr unit (fraction)

theorySlides.title: Grid vs Flexbox 🆚
theorySlides.content:
When to use which:

**Grid:** 2D layouts (rows AND columns)
• Page layouts
• Card grids
• Complex structures

**Flexbox:** 1D layouts (row OR column)
• Navigation bars
• Centering
• Single row/column

theorySlides.title: Responsive Grid
Grid Areas 🗺️

questions.question: What does 1fr mean?
questions.explanation: fr is a fraction unit for available space.

questions.question: What does auto-fit do in repeat()?
options: Fills row with as many columns as fit
questions.explanation: auto-fit creates as many columns as can fit in the available space.

questions.question: Which creates a 2x2 grid?
questions.explanation: Define both columns and rows with grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows.

theorySlides.content:
Two types:

codingChallenge.title: Pulse Animation
codingChallenge.description: Create a pulse animation that scales 1 to 1.1.

testCases.expectedOutput: 0% { transform: scale(1); } 50% { transform: scale(1.1); } 100% { transform: scale(1); }

theorySlides.title: Responsive Design 📱
theorySlides.content:
Apply different styles based on screen size.

Breakpoints:
• Mobile: < 768px
• Tablet: 768px - 1024px
• Desktop: > 1024px

theorySlides.title: Mobile First
theorySlides.content: Start with mobile, add desktop styles.

questions.question: What is mobile-first?
options: Write mobile CSS first, add desktop
questions.explanation: Mobile-first uses base styles for mobile, media queries for larger screens.
